The Council is responsible for a number of public open spaces and parks within the town and is committed to ensuring that these areas are maintained to a clean, tidy and high standard for the benefit of residents and visitors.
These green spaces are an important part of the town's community infrastructure, contributing to health, wellbeing and visual amenity.
The contract for South Road will include, but not be limited to, edging, grass cutting, weeding, planting of trees, shrubs and seasonal bedding, pruning, small tree works, sports pitch maintenance and any other grounds maintenance tasks as required.

This tender process forms part of Hythe Town Council's formal procurement arrangements for substantial works and services. Where the estimated contract value exceeds £25,000 net of VAT, the Council will comply with the relevant provisions of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 and the Local Government Act 1972, including publication requirements.
Submission of Tenders
Tender specifications and accompanying documentation will be provided to interested contractors on request. Please contact the Town Clerk in the first instance to obtain the full tender pack.
All sealed tenders must be received by post no later than 5.00 pm on 31 December 2026 and addressed to:
The Town Clerk
Town Council Offices
Oaklands
Stade Street
Hythe
Kent
CT21 6BG
The Council will notify all tenderers of the outcome in writing by 15 January 2027.

The scope of the Contract will include, but not be limited to: park and open space carriageway, car park and footpath reconstruction, drainage improvement works, play equipment inspection, repair, maintenance and replacement, public highway grass verge protection measures, the supply and installation of fencing and gates, wetland construction, flood alleviation and drainage projects, rain garden construction and planting, site investigations and trial excavations, and the supply and installation of planters, planting, turfing and topsoil. The scope will also include access through this contract to suppliers providing specialised and bespoke materials and play equipment.
The Supplier shall be responsible for providing all necessary management and supervision, labour, plant, equipment and materials required to deliver the works safely, efficiently and in accordance with project specific requirements.
The aim of this new contract is to provide opportunities to SME’s in the vicinity of the London Borough of Enfield that can provide socio-economic benefit to local people and local business.
The contract will provide a schedule of rates which will be used to deliver capital, revenue, and grant funding projects. The contract will cover multiple budgets and projects, and has no guaranteed contract spend. Therefore the financial breakdown changes annually and for every individual project.
The form of contract will be the ‘ICC Term Version August 2011 edition updated May 2015 with Special Conditions as added by the London Borough of Enfield.
The duration of the Contract will be 3 years with the option to extend up to 36 months or part thereof, subject to supplier performance and at the full discretion of the Authority.

• Sites shall be left clean, tidy and safe following each visit.

Pembrokeshire County Council on behalf of the South West Wales Corporate Joint Committee is developing the South West Wales DATGLOI Powering Cleaner Rivers project to explore how catchment-scale anaerobic digestion can support Wales’s climate change and nature recovery targets by bringing together agricultural nutrient management, renewable energy generation, river restoration and circular economy innovation within a single integrated model.
The project will focus on the potential development of anaerobic digestion infrastructure at a pilot site at Cwm Gwyrdd Nantycaws; the emerging circular economy park in Carmarthenshire. The study will assess how agricultural slurry, and other organic waste streams could be collected, processed and converted into renewable energy, while also supporting improved nutrient management in sensitive river catchments.
It will investigate how anaerobic digestion could improve slurry management, generate low-carbon energy, recover nutrients for reuse and export out of the catchment, reduce reliance on imported fertilisers, and support wider catchment recovery objectives. The project will also explore opportunities to process digestate into higher-value products, including potential biochar applications, creating further opportunities for carbon sequestration and circular economy development.
The purpose of this commission is to determine the technical, environmental, regulatory, commercial and financial viability of delivering catchment-scale anaerobic digestion and nutrient recovery infrastructure within the South West Wales region to solve multiple complex challenges.
The purpose of this commission is to:
1. Determine the technical, environmental, regulatory and commercial viability of a catchment-scale anaerobic digestion facility using Nantycaws/Cwm Gwyrdd as a pilot test site.
2. Assess the contribution that strategically planned nutrient recovery infrastructure could make towards nutrient neutrality, river restoration, climate mitigation and circular economy objectives.
3. Develop an investment-ready Outline Business Case that identifies preferred delivery, ownership and financing models.
4. Where additional funding is available, develop a replicable framework that can be applied across priority Welsh catchments.
5. Provide SWWCJC and partner authorities with a robust evidence base to support future investment decisions.
